name: How does mobile home flooring repair differ from standard home flooring repair?

mainEntity.name: How does mobile home flooring repair differ from standard home flooring repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mobile home flooring repair differs significantly from traditional homes because manufactured homes often feature particle board subflooring and lighter structural framing. In site-built homes, subfloors are typically thicker plywood or OSB attached to standard dimensional lumber joists. In mobile homes, plumbing lines, ductwork, and belly board insulation run directly beneath the subfloor panels. Improper cutting during repairs can damage these vital systems. Hiring a contractor familiar with mobile home structures ensures the belly wrap and sub-trades are protected while new, moisture-resistant subflooring and finish flooring are properly secured.
acceptedAnswer.description: Mobile homes use thinner framing and particle board subfloors over underlying ductwork and plumbing, requiring specialized cutting and framing techniques.
